lines.text: This is SolarLayout Rooftop, an app for designing rooftop PV systems in the browser.
On the home page, you paste the coordinates of the roof, or you search for an address.
When you click the building, the app detects its footprint, and you can drag the corners if you need to.
When you build the roof, it opens in 3D with the modules already laid out, and you can show the satellite imagery under it.
If you turn on the sun and play the day, the shadows move across the roof, and the shade on every module is worked out for the whole year.
On the array step, you choose the module, its tilt and the spacing of the rows.
On the strings step, the app chooses an inverter for this roof and compares the stringing options side by side.
Every hour of a typical year is simulated, each loss is listed, and you get the P50, P75 and P90 values.
The handover step gives you the report, the single-line diagram, the bill of materials, the cable schedule, and DXF and KMZ files.
For this roof, the result is one thousand one hundred and seventy-five megawatt hours a year.
It is free, with no account needed, at rooftop dot solarlayout dot app.
